findings.title: A legal marketplace named local is routed to direct-local plugin uninstall
findings.trigger: A valid marketplace has registry name local and a plugin is successfully installed from it; the ordinary state has no direct-local directory for that plugin name.
findings.expected: Use the marketplace uninstall route for its cached installation.
findings.actual: The catalog suffix is local, so resolver returns kind local and the UI calls uninstallLocalPlugin. Its direct-directory guard rejects rather than uninstalling the marketplace cache entry.
findings.cause: Allowed marketplace names and the direct-local origin marker share the same namespace and plugin@local identity, while the routing DTO/helper lacks a discriminating origin.
counterevidence: Actual direct-local marker behavior is intentional and must be preserved.
CSMeta/source and installPath exist, but the inspected catalog/helper routing does not use them to distinguish these origins.
Old truthy-local missing branch is the reverse-origin failure; R52 local version cache and PROFILE-R5-01 repo-key folding are separate causes.
findings.validation: Three attributed static source scopes plus metadata review; no product/helper/fixture/test, install/uninstall/catalog/existsSync/HTTP/native execution. No runtime observation or deletion/damage claim.
findings.remediation: Preserve an explicit installation origin through the producer/summary/helper contract, or consistently reserve/migrate the name; do not simply remove actual local-marker support.
findings.classificationNote: Root promotes this same candidate to one static P3 finding after supported ordinary input/entry and deterministic branch/callee proof. Original candidate/support records are unchanged; alias is not a second item.
